generated_sql:
WITH MonthlyRevenue AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id, 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, 
        SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS revenue
    FROM 
        public.orders o
    JOIN 
        public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    GROUP BY 
        o.customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)
),
CustomerOrderCount AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id, 
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
    FROM 
        public.orders
    GROUP BY 
        customer_id
),
RevenueGrowth AS (
    SELECT 
        mr.customer_id,
        MIN(mr.month) AS first_month,
        MAX(mr.month) AS last_month,
        MIN(mr.revenue) AS first_month_revenue,
        MAX(mr.revenue) AS last_month_revenue,
        (MAX(mr.revenue) - MIN(mr.revenue)) AS revenue_growth
    FROM 
        MonthlyRevenue mr
    GROUP BY 
        mr.customer_id
)
SELECT 
    c.customer_id, 
    c.company_name, 
    rg.first_month, 
    rg.last_month, 
    rg.first_month_revenue, 
    rg.last_month_revenue, 
    rg.revenue_growth
FROM 
    RevenueGrowth rg
JOIN 
    public.customers c ON rg.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN 
    CustomerOrderCount coc ON rg.customer_id = coc.customer_id
WHERE 
    coc.order_count >= 5
ORDER BY 
    rg.revenue_growth DESC
LIMIT 10;

question: Welche Produktpaare aus unterschiedlichen Kategorien werden ueberproportional oft gemeinsam gekauft (Lift gegenueber Unabhaengigkeit)?
generated_sql:
WITH product_pairs AS (
  SELECT 
    od1.product_id AS product_id1, 
    od2.product_id AS product_id2, 
    COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM 
    public.order_details od1
  JOIN 
    public.order_details od2 ON od1.order_id = od2.order_id AND od1.product_id < od2.product_id
  GROUP BY 
    od1.product_id, od2.product_id
),
product_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id, 
    COUNT(*) AS total_count
  FROM 
    public.order_details
  GROUP BY 
    product_id
),
lift_calculation AS (
  SELECT 
    pp.product_id1, 
    pp.product_id2, 
    pp.pair_count, 
    pt1.total_count AS total_count1, 
    pt2.total_count AS total_count2,
    (pp.pair_count::float / (pt1.total_count * pt2.total_count)) AS lift
  FROM 
    product_pairs pp
  JOIN 
    product_totals pt1 ON pp.product_id1 = pt1.product_id
  JOIN 
    product_totals pt2 ON pp.product_id2 = pt2.product_id
)
SELECT 
  p1.product_name AS product_name1, 
  p2.product_name AS product_name2, 
  lc.lift
FROM 
  lift_calculation lc
JOIN 
  public.products p1 ON lc.product_id1 = p1.product_id
JOIN 
  public.products p2 ON lc.product_id2 = p2.product_id
ORDER BY 
  lc.lift DESC
LIMIT 10;
